page: Microsoft Azure D96ls_v6 is a compute-focused general purpose virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processors operating at up to 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The configuration includes 192 GB of total system RAM, corresponding to a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core, alongside 260 MB of shared L3 cache and hardware acceleration flags such as AVX-512 and AMX matrix instructions.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded compute capability, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 21,482 and a PassMark CPU score of 86,191.93, both placing in the top 10 percent of tested systems. Multi-threaded stress-ng throughput and Clang software compilation also achieve strong tier ratings. While cached memory bandwidth reaches 6,201.65 GB/s, large-block uncached read and write bandwidths measure 257.01 GB/s and 107.31 GB/s respectively. Because the instance contains no local storage and zero integrated GPUs, storage I/O relies entirely on attached network storage volumes.

With a lower memory allocation per vCPU compared to standard general-purpose profiles, the D96ls_v6 provides high compute density without the overhead of unneeded memory capacity. This configuration offers balanced cost efficiency for highly parallel, CPU-bound workloads. Recommended use cases include large-scale CI/CD build farms, batch processing, static web serving clusters, and CPU-based machine learning prompt processing.
description: Microsoft Azure D96ls_v6 is a high-density compute instance configured with 96 vCPUs and 192 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio. Driven by dedicated 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processors with 260 MB of L3 cache, the system supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AMX. Multi-core performance is confirmed by top-tier results in PassMark CPU and Geekbench multi-core benchmarks, along with high static web serving throughput. The instance provides no bundled local storage and no GPU hardware, requiring remote storage volumes for persistent data. This resource allocation delivers cost-effective processing for CPU-intensive deployments that do not demand extensive RAM pools, such as distributed compilation pipelines, batch processing jobs, and high-throughput web front ends.
